title: Public talks & engagement
text:
I am passionate about sharing my knowledge of the Thames Estuary and its remarkable wildlife with wider audiences.
As a Chartered Marine Scientist with experience in lecturing, teaching and public engagement, I offer accessible and engaging talks exploring the ecology, biodiversity, environmental history and conservation of the Thames Estuary.
Drawing on my scientific research, professional experience and teaching background, I aim to make aquatic ecology accessible to audiences of all backgrounds.

Talk topics
Fishes and habitats of the Thames Estuary
Discover the fascinating underwater world of the Thames, its diverse fish communities and the importance of estuarine habitats in supporting aquatic biodiversity.
From pollution to recovery
Explore the environmental history of the Thames, its ecological recovery and the challenges facing this highly urbanised estuary.
Restoring the Thames
Discover how habitat restoration, conservation and nature-based solutions can support biodiversity and improve the ecological resilience of the Thames Estuary.


Audiences and events
I welcome invitations from:

Local societies and community groups
Universities and educational institutions
Museums and libraries
Environmental and conservation organisations
Professional organisations
Public event and festival organisers

Talks can be delivered in person or online and tailored to the interests and scientific background of the audience.

title: Wanda Bodnar
text:
I am a Chartered Marine Scientist with diverse professional experience across academia, the offshore industry and the charity sector. Since 2016, I have worked on aquatic habitat conservation, restoration and climate resilience projects in the Thames Estuary.
Alongside my scientific work, I have experience in lecturing, teaching and science communication, supported by a formal teaching qualification. I am passionate about making aquatic ecology accessible to wider audiences through public talks, educational activities and community engagement. I also lead ecology-focused stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) sessions, combining natural history education with outdoor activities.
I am currently a PhD researcher within the London NERC Doctoral Training Partnership, investigating the ecology of fish communities and the importance of intertidal habitats in the Thames Estuary.

title: Research
text:
My PhD focuses on fish community responses to intertidal habitat condition and restoration across the Thames Estuary.
Further information about my PhD project, research objectives, methodology and progress is available on my dedicated research website.
